winner.text: Add a categorical tab-by-hour interaction feature to the additive scorer.
winner.rationale: The current context-aware scorer has strong overall within-user discrimination (GAUC 0.668912) but weak top-five results in several large hour slices, including hour 16 nDCG@5 0.357042 and hour 14 nDCG@5 0.363601. A single causal context conjunction can model time-of-surface effects that separate tab and hour weights cannot express.
winner.exact_ablation: Add exactly one train-vocabulary categorical feature formed as the tuple (tab, hour) to experiment 1's existing additive user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday scorer; retain the model, binary loss, optimizer, regularization, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003 versus experiment 1, because tab-specific time effects may repair within-user inversions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 versus experiment 1, with greater potential than GAUC because the diagnosed deficit is concentrated at top five in context slices.

selection_rationale: c01 is the best next scarce experiment because it is the consultant's top-ranked option (utility 0.78) and offers a focused, low-risk test of an evidenced gap: large, sufficiently populated hour slices have weak top-five performance (hour 16 nDCG@5 0.357042 across 6,858 rows; hour 14 nDCG@5 0.363601 across 6,003 rows). It preserves the proven additive model and all training settings while adding only one leakage-safe, train-vocabulary interaction that can capture tab-specific temporal effects absent from separate main effects. Its expected primary gain of 0.002 is lower than broad architecture alternatives, but its higher reliability, low runtime cost, limited validation-overfitting exposure, and clean causal attribution make it preferable under a one-experiment budget.
